---
name: publish-game
description: "Publish, update or unpublish static HTML/JavaScript games on voyager.site."
---

Publish only when the user asks to publish or publicly share this game. Creating, previewing,
playtesting or preparing a game does not authorize publication. An explicit request to publish
now authorizes that selected release; do not add another confirmation ceremony. Updating a
public game and unpublishing also require the user's intent. Never publish a different folder
to work around a suspension.

Use the built-in `voyager game` commands, which use the user's existing Voyager sign-in.
Never ask for Cloudflare credentials, sign up for hosting, or put credentials in game files.
When publishing needs a Voyager sign-in, `voyager auth login --no-wait` opens it in the user's
browser; publish once they have signed in.

1. Build the static output and playtest it locally. Use [make-web-game](../make-web-game/SKILL.md)
   for creation and preview tools. Bundle ESM, styles, fonts, images, audio and JSON locally;
   use relative URLs (`./assets/...`, Vite `base: './'`). Hosting runs no backend code and gives
   the game no privileged Voyager bridge. Verify phone controls, resizing, restart and audio
   after a real user gesture. Keep a mute control.
2. Select the precise built folder containing `index.html`, such as `dist`. A selected single
   HTML file is published as `index.html` and includes no siblings unless a thumbnail is named.
   Do not select the whole repository or user home. A game with sibling dependencies needs its
   built folder selected explicitly.
3. A PNG/JPEG/WebP thumbnail is optional for general publishing. If none is selected, tell the
   user: **X will show a plain link card, not the playable game**. This warning does not add a
   confirmation step to an already authorized publication. For an X game, follow
   [make-x-game](../make-x-game/SKILL.md): its square poster with the title and "Tap to play" is
   required. With a thumbnail, Studio supplies `twitter:card=player`, a player URL of the stable
   root plus `?embed=1`, and a 480×480 frame. Build and test that embed mode; X still decides
   whether to play the card inline. Any site may embed the public game, not only X. Do not add
   player dimensions to the upload manifest.
4. Run `voyager game prepare --source-path ./dist --json`. For a thumbnail, also pass
   `--thumbnail-path poster.png` (relative to the selected folder). Review **every included
   path**, excluded paths, total bytes and returned `digest`. All included files become public.
   Hidden files, credentials, source maps, source folders and build configuration are excluded;
   symlinks, hardlinks, unsafe paths and case collisions are refused. Never put files or a folder
   named `_v` at the bundle root: that exact namespace is reserved for hosted versions. Nested
   `assets/_v/`, `_assets/` and `_v-game.js` are allowed. JavaScript delivered to a
   browser is public source: never embed private keys or tokens. Exclusions cannot detect every
   secret inside an otherwise valid asset. Literal missing asset references are refused;
   dynamically constructed references still need real playtesting.
5. For a first publication, pick a short readable slug for the game, such as `moon-hop`. Use
   1–40 lowercase ASCII letters/digits with single hyphens between words; no leading/trailing
   hyphen or `--`. Never use brand names or imply a misleading affiliation. The server adds the
   random six-character suffix automatically; do not invent or choose it. After verifying that
   the selected release matches the user's publishing intent, run
   `voyager game publish --source-path ./dist --title "Moon hop" --slug moon-hop --digest REVIEW_DIGEST --confirm-public --json`,
   replacing `REVIEW_DIGEST` with the exact value from prepare, and repeat the same thumbnail
   option if used. The service rebuilds and compares the snapshot before uploading. If anything
   changed, prepare/review again. Never bypass the digest check. `--slug` is optional and only
   applies when the game is first created; omit it on updates. If it differs from an existing
   game's slug, the service warns and keeps the permanent URL. Explain that warning rather than
   creating another game or changing the local source path.
6. Return the confirmed public root URL, controls and validation performed. URLs have the form
   `https://<slug>-<random6>.voyager.site`, for example `https://moon-hop-a2b3c4.voyager.site`.
   Always use the returned URL, never a guessed hostname. The document itself is playable and carries
   the title/thumbnail metadata; there is no separate landing page. Verify the public page when
   deployment is available. For X releases, follow the Twitterbot tag, player/poster HTTPS 200,
   and framing checks in [player-card.md](../make-x-game/references/player-card.md). Do not claim
   a link is live solely from a local preview or claim X playback from HTTP checks alone.

## Manage the same publication

To embed the game on a website, use its confirmed public root URL with `?embed=1`:

```html
<iframe
  src="https://ACTUAL_GAME_HOST.voyager.site/?embed=1"
  title="Game title"
  width="480"
  height="480"
  allow="autoplay; fullscreen"
></iframe>
```

Resize the frame for the host page and keep the game responsive. Embedding grants no Voyager
credentials or privileged bridge; the game's static hosting sandbox and network restrictions
still apply. X chooses whether to show its player card inline.

- `voyager game status --source-path ./dist --json` reads authoritative state.
- Publish again from the same source path and account to update the same URL. Rename with
  `voyager game rename --source-path ./dist --title "New title" --json` without reuploading.
  Rename changes the displayed title only; the original slug and URL are permanent.
- `voyager game unpublish --source-path ./dist --confirm-unpublish --json` stops new public
  requests within 30 seconds, including old version paths. Downloaded bytes cannot be revoked.
- After a timeout, check status before retrying. The saved random creation key and game ID are
  reused, so preserve the local publication receipt. Do not change the path/account to force a
  second creation. A build folder that was deleted can still be renamed or unpublished through
  its original path. Local receipts live in the Voyager profile, outside the public bundle.

Limits: 500 files, 10 MiB per file, 50 MiB unpacked, 30 MiB compressed ZIP. Supported assets and
path restrictions are reported by prepare. If a game exceeds these limits, optimize the built
assets or use another host the user requests.

Free accounts can have **two games live at once**. Updating an already live game preserves its
URL and uses the same slot. If the service reports HTTP 402 `free_game_limit`, explain it and let the
user choose which existing game to unpublish or offer [Voyager billing](https://voyager.so/dashboard/billing).
Never unpublish one automatically or create a new account/path to bypass the cap. Link the
existing billing entrypoint rather than inventing a plan, price, or checkout URL.

Free, Starter, and accounts without a plan receive a quick, permissive AI safety check before
activation. Plans above Starter skip content checks. Structural bundle validation applies to
every plan. If the AI check's rare content
refusal returns HTTP 422 `content_flagged`, show the service's reason verbatim and stop; do not automatically
retry, rewrite the game, or conceal content to pass. If the user asks to address the flagged
content, prepare and review the changed snapshot before another publish. A model outage or
timeout does not block publishing; the check fails open.
A content refusal or failed upload leaves the previous live version unchanged. For ordinary
upstream or transport errors, check status before retrying and report only confirmed results. Never hide
content from the check or reupload under another identity to bypass a refusal or suspension.

Publication, updates and title changes can take up to 20 seconds to become visible at an edge
location. Wait through that bounded cache window before diagnosing a stale response. Unpublish
retains its 30-second maximum for stopping new requests.

Voyager hosts static games and blocks external network connections. Shared live rooms need the
user's own server and hosting that permits connections to it. Do not offer a multiplayer server
on `voyager.site`; Cloudflare Pages is an alternative only when the user chooses their own host.

Sharing a URL does not promise inline X playback. X decides how links appear; the game always
has its directly playable browser URL. Do not post to X or another account unless asked.
Report abuse through Voyager support with the root game URL; operators can suspend a game.
